Date: 2021-05-14
REMARKS
This communication is responsive to the Office Action dated March 16, 2021. Applicant has not amended the claims. Claims 1-26 remain pending.
Claim Reiection Under 35 U.S.C. 102
The Office Action rejected claims 1 and 13 under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by U.S. Patent Application No. 8,855,755 by Zhang et al. (hereinafter, "Zhang"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejections. Zhang fails to disclose all of the elements of the claims, as required by 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1), and provides no apparent reason for modification to include such features.
For example, as argued in the previous Amendment, Zhang fails to disclose or suggest processing circuitry configured to "for each of the plurality of ventricular depolarizations, identify a maximum slope point, a minimum slope point, and an interval from the maximum slope point to the minimum slope point," as recited by independent claim 1, or the similar features of independent claim 13.
The Office cited col. 11, 11. 7-14 and col. 13, 11. 61-63 of Zhang as allegedly disclosing these features. However, Zhang does not describe that analysis of "NR-R intervals to determine whether sudden rate onset is present" described at col. 11, 11. 7-14 means that the slope peak shift (SPS) described at col. 13, 11. 61-63 is determined for NR-R intervals. To the contrary, Zhang states "In any case, processor 70 may better discriminate treatable arrhythmias from non- treatable arrhythmias by performing morphology analysis on a single beat instead of using extensive processing resources to do morphology analysis on a plurality of beats." Furthermore, while Zhang discloses that "processor 70 performs the morphology analysis of the onset initiation beat by analyzing one or more beat morphology parameters,"2 Zhang fails to disclose or suggest a medical system comprising processing circuitry configured to identify "for each of the plurality of ventricular depolarizations... an interval from the maximum slope point to the minimum slope point" as recited in claim 1. Indeed, the closest Zhang comes to disclosing a minimum slope point appears to be its discussion of S2.3 Even assuming arguendo 1 Zhang, col. 12, 11. 63-67.
2 Zhang, col. 13, 11. 50-54.
3See Zhang, col. 17, 11. 15-21.
that S2 in FIG. 5 is an identified minimum slope point, which Applicant does not concede, Zhang only discloses S2 with respect to "an R-wave symmetry index (RSI) that represents the ratio of onset-side slope to offset-side slope of the R-wave in the far-field EGM,"4 which is not "an interval from the maximum slope point to the minimum slope point," as recited in claim 1.
This conclusion is reinforced by the fact that "[t]he RSI is computed as the absolute value of the ratio of the peak value of the onset-side slope to the peak value of the offset-side slope of the far-field EGM multiplied by the factor of 10,"5 whereas Applicant's originally-filed specification describes that "[p]rocessing circuitry 50 may determine the time interval, e.g., number of samples, also referred to herein as the slope interval, between the point of the maximum slope and the point of the minimum slope for each of depolarizations 122B-122D."6 "An absolute value of the ratio of the peak value of the onset-side slope to the peak value of the offset-side slope of the far-field EGM" is not the same as an interval from the maximum slope point to the minimum slope point. As such, to the extent that Zhang discloses processing circuitry configured to identify a minimum slope point, Zhang still fails to disclose or suggest processing circuitry configured to identify "for each of the plurality of ventricular depolarizations... an interval from the maximum slope point to the minimum slope point" as recited in claim 1.
For at least the reasons discussed above, independent claims 1 and 13 are patentable over Zhang. The dependent claims, i.e., claims 2-12 and 14-26 incorporate the requirements of the respective independent claims.7 Accordingly, the dependent claims are likewise patentable. Applicant therefore respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of this rejection.

Claim Reiection Under 35 U.S.C. 103
The Office Action rejected claims 2-12 and 14-26 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as follows:
" Claims 2-9 and 14-21 were rejected as allegedly being unpatentable over Zhang, in view of Sarkar, U.S. Patent Application No. 9,675,270 by Sarkar (hereinafter, "Sarkar");
" Claims 10 and 22 were rejected as allegedly being unpatentable over Zhang, in view of Sarkar, and further in view of U.S. Patent Application No. 7,751,876 by Healey (hereinafter, "Healey");
" Claims 11 and 12 were rejected as allegedly being unpatentable over Zhang, in view of Cao et al., U.S. Patent Application No. 7,027,858 by Cao et al. (hereinafter, "Cao"); and " Claims 23-26 were rejected as allegedly being unpatentable over Sarkar, in view of Healey.
Applicant respectfully traverses the rejections. The applied references, alone or in any combination, fail to disclose or suggest the features defined by Applicant's claims, and there would have been no apparent reason that would have caused one of ordinary skill in the art to modify the applied references to arrive at the claimed features.
For example, as discussed above, Zhang fails to disclose or suggest processing circuitry configured to identify "for each of the plurality of ventricular depolarizations... an interval from the maximum slope point to the minimum slope point" as recited in claim 1. Sarkar, Healey, and Cao, alone or in any proper combination, do not cure this deficiency or the other deficiencies of Zhang, nor were Sarkar, Healey, and Cao cited for this purpose.
For at least the reasons discussed above, claims 2-12, and 14-26 are patentable over Zhang in view of Sarkar, Healey, and Cao, alone or in any proper combination. Applicant therefore respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of this rejection.
CONCLUSION
All claims in this application are in condition for allowance. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and prompt allowance of all pending claims.
Applicant does not concede that the subject matter encompassed by the claims prior to this Response is unpatentable over the art cited by the Office. While several distinctions have been noted over the art of record, Applicant notes that there may be several other limitations that are neither taught nor suggested by the art of record. Applicant expressly reserves all rights and arguments with respect to distinctions not explicitly noted herein. In addition, to the extent that amendments included herein constitute a narrowing of the claims, such narrowing of the claims should not be construed as an admission as to the merits of the prior rejections. Indeed, Applicant traverses the rejections and preserves all rights and arguments. To the extent that any particular statement or argument by the Office has not been explicitly addressed herein, the same should not be construed as an acquiescence or admission by the Applicant that such statements or arguments by the Office are accurate and proper.
Please charge any additional fees or credit any overpayment to deposit account number 50-1778. The Examiner is invited to telephone the below-signed attorney to discuss this application.
